title: Miri Standard Agent Integration Event
description:
The request a host sends to an agent-integration binding when a trigger fires (Agent Integration Contract §3.2). The response is a discovery-envelope-v1 document carrying a `findings` payload key.

Note the deliberate asymmetry with discovery-envelope-v1.json, whose root is OPEN. That root is open because a new operation adds a payload key and a closed root would forbid it on the day it lands. This root is CLOSED for the opposite reason: the contract's §3.2 forbids an event carrying a file path, a diff, a buffer, or the user's source, and a closed object is what makes that prohibition mechanical rather than advisory. A host that cannot express its event without adding a field is a host reaching for the user's code.

schema_version.description: Wire-schema version of this event. An integer string — "1", "2" — compared numerically, matching every other schema_version in the standard.

kind.description: The observable moment, from the closed set in Agent Integration Contract §3.1. Closed for the same reason the servable set and the error codes are closed: two bindings that disagree about what an event is do not interoperate.

phase.description: Whether the action that produced the event has landed. `runtime.error` is necessarily `after`. `dependency.add` is `after` for a local surface: a package that is not yet installed ships nothing readable, so the earliest moment 3.5 can be performed is after the install and before any code is written against it — still before the decision that is expensive to reverse, since an install is undone with an uninstall and a codebase written against a package is not. `before` remains legal so a registry-side surface is not forbidden in advance. Every other kind is `before`.

subject.description: What the event is about, and nothing else. Closed by design: §3.2 forbids a file path, a diff, a buffer or the user's source, and a binding that needs the user's code to decide what to say has left this standard's scope and entered the host's.

package.description: The import package name, matching the Discovery Contract §3.0 grammar so an event can be passed to an operation without re-validation.

version.description: A version or version specifier, where the kind implies one. Carried as written; this contract does not parse it.

symbol.description: A dotted qualified name, where the kind implies one (runtime.error naming a failing surface, test.author naming the surface under test).

allOf.$comment: Agent Integration Contract §3.2 — runtime.error is necessarily `after`; it reports something that has already happened.

§3.2 — only `runtime.error` and `dependency.add` may be `after`. runtime.error reports something that has happened; dependency.add is `after` because a not-yet-installed package is not readable by a local surface. Every other kind fires while its action is still a proposal. This was found by an implementer building the first binding: the schema previously required every REQUIRED kind to be `before` and so rejected the only behavior a local surface can produce.
§3.1 — dependency.version_change is about a version, so it carries one. Without this a binding could fire the kind with nothing to distinguish it from dependency.add.
